summary: Douglas County, OR: 1930 crow's nest on a lookout tree at Umpqua NF; abandoned in the 1950s, cabin destroyed 1965; last description 2007 says tree standing.

facts.design: Crow's nest on a lookout tree (110 feet per firelookout.com); one-room shake-sided lookout dwelling built 1922
facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says the crow's nest was still there in the 1980s; Forest Lookouts says the lookout tree was still standing in 2007; FFLA lists it as abandoned. No later description found

corrections.why: Forest Lookouts calls the structure a lookout tree ('The lookout tree is still standing', 2007). The vocabulary's 'tree' is a lookout tree or tree platform, which fits better than an open platform.

The FFLA Oregon list shows Callahan Mountain as Abandoned, not Gone. Firelookout.com says the crow's nest was still there in the 1980s and Forest Lookouts says the tree stood in 2007. No source says it is gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list says Abandoned; firelookout.com says still there in the 1980s; Forest Lookouts says the lookout tree was standing in 2007. The brief's gone and standing labels both overstate the evidence, so status is set to unknown.
The 1922 date belongs to the one-room lookout dwelling in Forest Service files; the 1930 date is the crow's nest on the lookout tree. Both are kept as separate events.

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on the current state and do not describe the site after 2007. The brief's height (6.1 m) is not confirmed: firelookout.com gives a 110-foot crow's nest, which may be the platform height on the tree rather than the structure, so height is left out of facts until someone checks. The brief's conflict note says firelookout.com lists the site as standing, but that page says the crow's nest was still there in the 1980s, which is weaker. The brief's 1930 build date matches firelookout.com; the 1922 dwelling date comes from Forest Lookouts. A Facebook post by the Umpqua National Forest (Callahan lookout tree, 1930 photo) appeared in search, but the page returned no text, so it is not cited. The firelookout.com photo already in the record is not a new find. Next step: ask the Umpqua National Forest about the current state of the lookout tree and the site's access.
